meta.title: Logs, traces and execution lineage: scenario by scenario
meta.question: After an autonomous production action, what can each observation layer reconstruct and prove? For every scenario and every layer: what went in, what came out, the thirteen answers against ground truth, every recorded step, and where each number came from.
claim: Every scenario, read three ways from the same run.
Every answer scored against the systems of record.

variants.name: Application logs
variants.policy: each component's own log with its own ids (incident id where known, X-Request-Id propagated), trace ids removed, plus the approval service's tables

variants.name: Logs + traces
variants.policy: the same log lines with trace and span ids, plus every OpenTelemetry span of every process (standard GenAI and HTTP conventions)

variants.name: Execution lineage
variants.policy: hash-chained evidence events keyed by execution, action and attempt; witness anchors; the deployment API's transaction lookup by idempotency key

head: The experiment contract
rows: Governed execution lineage reconstructs an autonomous production change more completely than application logs or logs plus traces, and stays correct through crashes, retries, lost responses and tools that lie.

One execution per scenario. The action path is shared: the same policy, approvals, checkpoints, retries and idempotency. The governed path adds one behaviour: it reads the world back before declaring success.
What the investigator may read: L0 application logs (trace ids removed) · L1 the same logs with trace context plus every span · L2 the evidence events, witness anchors and the transaction lookup.
The deployment API's and approval service's own databases and the scenario pins: never the records being scored.
Thirteen questions per row: correct · partial (some parts not recorded) · not recorded · wrong · ambiguous. Joins counted as key joins or timestamp heuristics.
L2's completeness is by design: a coverage test, not a benchmark. Survival under injected failures is the experiment. Idempotency makes a retry safe; lineage makes it explainable.

blocks.title: How a row's outcome is decided
blocks.text: Each scenario runs once and is read three ways. An investigator per layer answers thirteen questions (trigger, principal and delegation, agent, model and configuration, policy version, approval, approver, capability, attempts, side effect, number of changes, real mitigation, integrity) from that layer alone, and each answer is scored against the deployment API's and approval service's own databases and the scenario pins. Held: all thirteen correct. Qualified: some answers missing or partial, none false. Broken: the layer recorded an answer that is false. A coverage test, not a benchmark: the lineage was designed to capture these facts; the failure scenarios test whether it survives. Correct answers in total: logs 149, logs + traces 149, lineage 195, each out of 195. Preregistered expectations held 68/68; predictions 7/7.
